sentences.text:
Present petition under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing of FIR at Crime No.
14/2021 registered at Police Station Mahila Police Station, Vidisha, District Vidisha (M.P.) for offence under Sections 498 (A) and 34 of IPC and section 3,4 of Dowry Prohibition Act as well as its consequential proceedings.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Police Station, Vidisha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, respondent No. 2 / complainant / Pooja W/o Shri Luv Kush Yadav on 24/09/2021 filed a written complaint stating therein that the marriage of complainant and her husband was solemnized as per Hindu Rites and Rituals in the year 2018.
After marriage, they are blessed with a son namely Hrdyansh.
After the birth of son Hrdyansh, in-laws of the complainant started harassing her for the demand of Jeep and house.
Complainant told her husband that her father is not economically sound and they cannot afford to fulfil the demand.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22041 2 MCRC-32746-2023
Further allegation levelled is that two year before the FIR lodged, in- laws of the complainant made complainant got out of the matrimonial house.

As the complainant was ousted from her matrimonial house by the in-laws, therefore, since then she is living in her parental home and none from her in-laws came to took her back to her matrimonial house.

It is further stated that the complainant tried to come back Ramraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170294528/
1 to her matrimonial house, but husband and in-laws used to beat the complainant.

sentences.text: The son of the complainant is living with the husband and her husband do not allow her to meet their child.
Upon the complaint, an FIR was registered against the present petitioners and other co-accused person U/s 498A, 34 of IPC and section 3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioners are living separately from the complainant and her husband which is evident from Ration card and the application filed by the petitioner No. 1 to police authority.
It is further argued that application before the authority on 07/10/2021 for proper investigation along with relevant documents have also been filed.
Petitioners have been arrayed in this case on the basis of false, frivolous and vexatious grounds.
The petitioners are living separately from the complainant and her husband and there was no direct or indirect involvement of the petitioners into the day to day affairs of the complainant.
On these grounds, it is prayed that the FIR registered against the petitioners deserves to be quashed.

On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the petition and argued that specific allegations have been made against the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22041 3 MCRC-32746-2023 petitioners.

The defence of the petitioners about filing application before the authority cannot be examined by this Court because same is subject matter of the evidence and can be decided by the learned trial court after taking evidence.
Under these circumstances, the instant petition deserves to be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the available record.
The perusal of the record indicates that complainant has made specific allegations against the petitioners about harassment for demand of dowry.
By filing documents, petitioners have raised their defence about their separate living and complaint made against the complainant.

The Apex Court in the case of Ajay Kumar Das vs. State of Jharkhand; (2011) 12 SCC 319 held that power of quashing of criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases for the Court would not be justified in embarking upon an inquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the first information report or in the complaint and that the extraordinary or the inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the Court to act according to whim or caprice."

entities.text: Ajay Kumar Das vs. State of Jharkhand; (2011) 12 SCC 319
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that the High Court when approached for quashing of a criminal proceeding should not appreciate the defence of the accused.

The Apex Court in the case of Padal Venkata RamaReddy Vs. Kovuri NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:22041 4 MCRC-32746-2023 Satyanarayana Reddy; (2012) 12 SCC 437 held that in a proceeding under Section 482, the High Court will not enter into any finding of facts.

Padal Venkata RamaReddy Vs. Kovuri NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:22041 4 MCRC-32746-2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These powers are neither limited nor curtailed by any other provisions of the Code.
However, such inherent powers are to be exercised sparingly, carefully and with caution.

sentences.text: Further, the Apex Court in the case of State of M.P. vs. Kunwar Singh by order dated 30.6.2021 passed in r.A. No. 709/2021 held that a detailed and meticulous appreciation of evidence at the stage of 482 of Cr.P.C. is not permissible and should not be done.

entities.text: State of M.P. vs. Kunwar Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Apex Court in the aforesaid case held as under:-
"8....
At this stage, the High Court ought not to be scrutinizing the material in the manner in which the trial court would do in the course of the criminal trial after evidence is adduced.
In doing so, the High Court has exceeded the well-settled limits on the exercise of the jurisdiction under Section 482 of CrPC.
A detailed enquiry into the merits of the allegations was not warranted.
The FIR is not expected to be an encyclopedia."

In the case of Rishipal Singh Vs State of U.P. And Another A.I.R. 2014 S.C.2567, the Apex court has laid down that while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. before quashing of complaint at the initial stage, the tests to be applied by the Court is as to whether the uncontroverted allegations as made in the complaint prima facie establish the offence.

entities.text: Rishipal Singh Vs State of U.P. And Another A.I.R. 2014 S.C.2567
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of above settled principles of law, since specific allegations have been levelled against the petitioners in respect to offence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:22041 5 MCRC-32746-2023 under Sections 498 (A) and 34 of IPC and section 3,4 of Dowry Prohibition Act,
this Court does not find it fit to quash the FIR at Crime No. 14/2021 registered at Police Station Mahila Police Station, Vidisha, District Vidisha (M.P.) for offence under Sections 498 (A) and 34 of IPC and section 3,4 of Dowry Prohibition Act against the present petitioners.

entities.text: Police Station Mahila Police Station, Vidisha
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Accordingly, present petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
